2026-11-27 · All platforms · Open-source software

The edition has 105 complete guides and 16 screened discoveries. It completes 27 earlier pending guides and details 1 substantive release updates. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 67 fields, 434/434 repository-query attempts and 24 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 434 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed queries, with 100 bounded. The model lane recorded 1 failed tasks. Metadata from 570 saved repository pages included 19,584 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 126,598 candidates, including pilot history and 1,043 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. One advertised Blender texture extension had a license text in its documentation repository, but no matching implementation there. The separate download could not be verified as covered by that grant and stays outside the edition. The reviewed AI Score Studio CLI defines a rule-based notation example. Its model-backed workflows remain on the roadmap, so the package stays outside the edition. Live primary research yielded 480 complete usable responses from 544 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 67 fields. 2 captures reached the size bound and 62 other sources were inaccessible or unusable. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 106 Quality unverified, 15 Experimental. Independent use remains unverified for 115 entries. The creative result check remains unverified for 120, and model, service or cost requirements remain unverified for 121. Repository searches returned no saved rows for Learned film, tape and audio restoration, Embodied and tactile interactive art, Multiband art and heritage imaging, Narrated and tactile exhibition interfaces, Learned shot matching and grading. Primary web research for these fields is included in the coverage notes. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: VeneraX (Quality unverified to Experimental), Comic Translation (Quality unverified to Experimental), 8f4e (Quality unverified to Experimental), PhotoCraft AI Diffusion (Quality unverified to Experimental), 3D Filmmaking Multimodal Evals (Experimental to Quality unverified). 23 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. Direct candidate source captures covered 214 identities. This edition includes 31 tools first retained by the historical pilot. Initial captures awaiting full source assessment and unsuccessful source attempts remain in local research. Model search gaps: text-to-image. The field notes identify the separate primary-source follow-up. All saved model-task results were screened as metadata, covering 1,150 rows and 1,150 distinct model identities. The separate watchlist made 71 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 1 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Search and review counts

67 creative fields; 434/434 repository queries attempted; 24/24 model-task queries attempted. 21950 distinct source candidates and 1039 model leads. 105 detailed profiles and 16 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 100 bounded repository queries, 1 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

Today’s field coverage

FieldFinding
Images & designComfyUI’s primary FLUX text-to-image tutorial documents current generation inputs and model choices. Invoke describes an editable image canvas with region-based generation. The image-to-image task documentation distinguishes transformation of an input image from generation using a text prompt alone. Split image-to-image inference from the layer or canvas editing interface. Save the source, output and model choice so a later color or composition pass is reproducible. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Video, animation & filmThe LibreAIFrames publisher shows RIFE frame interpolation with scene-cut handling. FilmCraft publishes a separate nonlinear timeline whose native speech route has its own dependencies. Frame interpolation and timeline editing solve different stages. Compare generated inbetweens over a hard cut and retain the original timing. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Audio, music & voiceThe Faust project documents routing and signal-processing integrations. The audio-to-audio model task lists learned transforms such as source separation and enhancement. An audio-to-audio model can transform an existing track while the DSP layer handles routing. Keep processed and dry stems aligned for comparison. 4 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
3D, reconstruction & assetsThe Gaussian splatting authors optimize a representation from photographed views for novel-view rendering. FreeCAD documents a solid-model handoff that requires reconstructing editable geometry. A learned view-synthesis representation and editable parametric solids serve different downstream tasks. Preserve separate scene captures and design solids. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Browser tools & web mediaMediaPipe documents image, video and live-stream hand-landmark modes for web JavaScript. MDN describes the separate WebGPU adapter and device interfaces. The web hand-landmark guide documents client inference inputs and outputs. The WebGPU specification surface depends on browser and device support. Source 1 Source 2
WebXR, VR & ARThe Immersive Web material documents runtime access to headset input and display. Depth model documentation describes the map that can supply a separate stereo reconstruction stage. Separate the immersive rendering and interaction interface from the model used to produce or interpret an asset. Verify the actual browser and headset route. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Computational art & creative codingMediaPipe’s browser hand landmarker exposes normalized landmark coordinates. Those coordinates can be read by a creative patch without handing the model control of the renderer. Hand landmark coordinates can drive a creative coding sketch. Calibrate input coordinate scaling and hold a recoverable neutral state when tracking drops. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Interactive, immersive & live mediaField 4’s example exposes learned speech embeddings as data available to a live audio and image patch. A live patch can map learned speech representations to scene controls. Test the mapping with likely performers and keep an editable scene. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
3D printing & generative CADFabDreamer’s authors describe semantic mask selection and layered design edits for laser-cut artwork. FreeCAD documents an independent route for measurable fabricated parts. Review generated parametric dimensions and geometry in a solid modeler before any physical cut or print. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Games & production pipelinesThe audio-generation task supplies candidate game sounds. Godot’s WAV resource documents loop endpoints and playback settings for using those assets in the engine. Generated clips still need looping, trim and import checks inside the game engine. Keep editable sound sources and engine-ready copies. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Motion capture & character animationMediaPipe’s pose-landmarker guide describes image and world landmarks. CozyClay materials provide a separate, editable character and camera staging workflow. Pose inference and animation authoring generate different intermediate data. Check rotation, contact and frame cadence before retargeting. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Avatars, digital humans & lip syncThe Blender extension registry documents generating facial keys from spoken phonemes, with language-specific Vosk model selection in a separate dependency. The Blender lip-sync extension uses Vosk speech models and can produce editable keys. Select the model for the dialogue language and inspect consonants after baking. Source 1 Source 2
VFX, compositing & relightingThe light-aware compositing authors describe carrying image-dependent lighting into a composite. The related capture literature scopes where learned geometric estimates come from. Lighting-aware compositing and coarse learned geometry require shot-specific checks. Keep separate lighting, matte and source layers for revision. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Spatial audio & volumetric mediaFAST-RIR’s authors model a diffuse room response conditioned on acoustic inputs. Open Spatial Delay documents a different layer, applying spatial routing and channel handling in a plugin. Scene-conditioned audio generation still needs a spatial routing stage. Verify the channel convention and playback decoder separately. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Photogrammetry, scanning & neural renderingINRIA’s Gaussian splatting project provides the camera-view training method. The Blender developer notes discuss the data and rendering stages needed to bring splats into an editor. Neural view synthesis depends on a set of consistent views. Keep original cameras and an interchange copy of the learned scene. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Editing, captions & post-productionThe OpenTimelineIO project documents a representation of clips, gaps and time. A video assistant that proposes cuts still needs an explicit mapping from these decisions to editor media and timing. Agent-directed edits need a transferable timeline. Reopen cuts in the finishing editor to check source-media relinking and timebase. 15 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Vector graphics, illustration & texturesThe SVG specification defines paths, coordinates and presentation attributes. SVGRender’s model materials are evidence for a separate learned vector-generation step. Vector model output can contain difficult paths or raster layers. Inspect editable curves, fill orientation and text before print export. Source 1 Source 2
Typography, fonts & layoutCounterpunch documents an optional assistant inside a glyph editor. FontForge documents editable glyph and font data for comparing what the assistant produces. The assistant in a font editor can aid glyph scripting. Maintain editable font sources and check spacing, script coverage and extrema. Source 1 Source 2
Storyboarding, narrative & comicsThe Drama AI project’s creative scope includes scene planning. CozyClay documents a stage where blocking and camera choices stay revisable. Separate scene planning from final renders. A creator can retain shots, actor blocking and source prompts as editable decisions. Source 1 Source 2
Creative publishing & presentationThe document-parser package describes structured extraction from source pages. The local caption package exposes the separate speech-timing route for editorial media. Structure extraction and speech timestamps can support editorial handoff. Proof reading order and text identity before publication. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Photography, restoration & colorPelli and FormDAM describe distinct parts of a shoot review, automated selection and semantic retrieval. The original ratings and camera files remain the reference for checking both. Photo culling and semantic search belong at different points in the selection workflow. Keep original RAW files and inspect selected and rejected frames. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Data art & scientific visualizationThe cited research and the MIT Media Lab’s Illuminate materials provide two places to check how data can become a visible mapping in a designed experience. When learned data supplies an art visualization, retain the raw observations and state how the model transforms the visual encoding. Source 1 Source 2
Physical, robotic & kinetic installationsThe MIT Media Lab publishes an example of sensing in a physical installation. The hand-landmarker guide provides a specific learned sensor output available for patching. Contact-free sensing can feed physical or projected media. Rehearse latency, lighting and the fallback behavior with the actual installation. Source 1 Source 2
Performance, projection & stage mediaThe IRCAM project documents using learned musical agents during composition and improvisation. Field 4 exposes speech embedding data to a separate performance patch. Map learned audio features to separate live cues and record a rehearsal trace before relying on the mapping on stage. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Fashion, textiles & wearable mediaThe OpenTryOn authors document garment-conditioned image synthesis. Editable measurements and garment templates live in a separate pattern authoring environment. Try-on synthesis previews a look. Pattern pieces, dimensions and physical fit require their own editable artifacts and validation. Source 1 Source 2
Accessible media & assistive creationW3C documents when a video needs descriptions of visual action. The linked publisher caption workflow produces dialogue text with a separate human review requirement. Automatic speech captions and descriptive narration cover different information needs. Review timed text and relevant visual events separately. 2 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Mobile, edge & on-device creationF-Droid exposes an app distribution scoped to phone-side audio processing. The Android MediaPipe guide shows that model setup is its own mobile dependency. A phone-side workflow depends on device-specific model and media support. Check storage, export and offline behavior on the chosen device. 3 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Creative learning & authoringManim Voiceover documents interchangeable speech services that can be used while keeping classroom animation in an editable scene. Maintain scene scripts and narration timing as teaching assets. A speech service and a 3D learning project carry separate deployment requirements. Source 1 Source 2
Archives, media restoration & collectionsArkindex and eScriptorium describe document regions and transcription as data aligned with digitized source pages. Both prompt preserving the underlying facsimile. Transcribe digitized texts into a separately editable layer. Retain originals and record the OCR and reading-order corrections. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Emerging & cross-disciplinary creative AIThe image-text-to-text task describes a model accepting mixed image and language inputs. That interface can support tagged asset review with a retained image-to-comment link. Model-assisted nodes can connect image, text and audio operations. Keep enough intermediate state to review and replace each dependency. Source 1
Hand-drawn and cutout animation inbetweensThe ToonCrafter authors and LibreAIFrames publisher show learned tools for making new frames from given drawings or video. Their examples use distinct input and timing assumptions. RIFE-style interpolation and learned cartoon inbetweens are distinct routes. Compare held frames, large pose changes and line stability on a short cel sequence. Source 1 Source 2
Layered illustration and cutout riggingLive2D documents editable cutout hierarchies. A separate pose landmarker provides observations a rigging workflow could map to selected controls. Keep the layered artwork and the rig separate when learned pose or interpolation drives a cutout. Maintain a reference pose for re-alignment. Source 1 Source 2
Comic lettering and editable panelsThe Japanese manga OCR project describes recognition inside dialogue crops. Keeping the source crop associated with the recognized line makes relettering reviewable. OCR can extract dialogue from panels for lettering. Verify reading order and characters before replacing original balloon artwork. Source 1
Multiband art and heritage imagingThe MIRA author documents aligning multiband heritage photography. Its registration step can be paired with a separately documented learned transcription layer when a source contains writing. MIRA documents multiband registration for heritage photography. Its development process alone does not establish end-user AI inference. Preserve registration references when pairing scans with learned transcription. Source 1 Source 2
Spatial soundfield reconstructionThe cited spatial plugin and authors’ room-response research establish different points of a route from estimated acoustic response to Ambisonic or binaural audition. The spatial plugin documents ambisonic and binaural output routes. Neural generation upstream and decoder compatibility downstream require independent checks. Source 1 Source 2
Scene-aware sound design and game audioSoundSpaces documents geometrical simulation of acoustics. Scene2Sound presents a learned approach to assigning sound to visual scene objects. Scene-conditioned sound design can use learned generation or spatial simulation. Keep coordinates and generated audio as separate authoring controls. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Live digital puppetry and stage charactersThe Blender extension registry describes phoneme animation. The web hand-landmarker guide describes a separate control signal for expressive puppets. Landmark and speech-driven workflows produce different puppet controls. Verify behavior during occlusion and silence before live use. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Multi-camera performance captureFreeMoCap’s maintainer documentation describes processing synchronized multi-camera recordings. Its context makes calibration and downstream retargeting explicit. Multi-camera pose capture depends on calibration and visible actors. Keep camera and skeleton data for checking retargeted movement. Source 1 Source 2
Editable rough cuts and media interchangeRelo presents an agent-directed video assembly workflow. OpenTimelineIO supplies a documented interchange target against which to check time and source links. Store model-assisted cut decisions on an editable timeline with original clips. Verify handles, timebase and relinking after the first export. 2 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Field recording and archival audio taggingCornell and the companion package document learned bird-call identification and timestamps, which a sound artist can use as an index into source recordings. Learned acoustic labels can index long field recordings. Keep confidence and offsets and review rare events against the original clip. Source 1 Source 2
Museum access and exhibition authoringZKM’s Beyond Matter release describes mixed exhibition contexts. W3C’s description guidance gives a separate specification for the accessible media inside an exhibit. ZKM documents a hybrid exhibit staging workflow. W3C describes separate visual description choices. An editable exhibition needs source records and accessible narration. Source 1 Source 2
AI-assisted contact sheets and photography proofingFormDAM documents searchable photo collections. Pelli presents a culling workflow that can be evaluated on a fixed copy of an existing shoot. Model-assisted proofing ranks or retrieves photos. Review decisions on a copy of the shoot and keep the original catalog and ratings available. Source 1 Source 2
Vector cleanup and printmaking preparationSVG’s path and transform rules give an editable target for a learned segmentation or vectorization stage. Record which shapes remain raster before preparing a print plate. Inspect a learned vector result at output size. Check path continuity, fills and lettering before splitting the art into separations. Source 1 Source 2
Costume patterns and garment prototypingOpenTryOn exposes learned visualization of garments on people. Seamly provides a documented stage for construction outlines and measurements. Keep authored measurements separate from generated try-on previews. Fit and sewing allowances depend on the editable pattern. Source 1 Source 2
Studio fabrication, surfaces and editable CAD3DCraft’s examples show a model-assisted route to parametric shape creation. ParCAD documents a separately editable solid model. Use measurable parametric outputs as the handoff from model-assisted form ideas. Manuscript layout and marginalia transcriptioneScriptorium works from scanned documents and PAGE XML documents the region geometry and text ordering that can be exported for scholarly revision. Mobile dailies and offline creative reviewThe documented mobile captioning route can supply timed review text. A device-specific listing does not guarantee the same media import or export behavior on another platform. Export short review material and separate timed text when possible. Confirm each mobile and desktop route explicitly. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Portable web scenes and point cloud viewersSPZ documents a compact splat representation. WebGPU documentation describes the separate viewer prerequisites that determine whether an atlas can render it. A browser scene's model data, compression format and rendering support are separate. Keep the high-detail source and check the actual target browser. Source 1
Neural materials and editable lightingThe light-aware compositing paper describes learned lighting estimates. Blender’s Principled shader documentation exposes material settings that can remain editable during the handoff. Validate a learned lighting or material result with neutral lighting and preserve editable roughness, color and normal inputs where available. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Literate creative coding and node authoringThe Script TOP documentation identifies callable transform hooks. Field 4’s embeddings example shows model output that can be connected to an authored script. Document the model input and output schema inside the patch or sketch. Save a non-live draft to inspect mappings and dependencies. Source 1 Source 2
Adaptive levels and game authoringThe published level-generation project describes learned layouts. Godot navigation documents a separate practical check for characters moving through a generated scene. Generated game spaces need explicit playability checks in the target engine. Keep scene geometry and navigation separate from prompt history. Source 1 Source 2
Multilingual spoken-book productionThe source packages describe chapter-based speech generation. Retaining paragraphs and chapter ordering makes later re-recording possible without regenerating the whole book. Keep chapter text, narration settings and rendered audio separate. Review pronunciation and chapter transitions with the source manuscript. Source 1 Source 2
Editable performance and music controlsBasic Pitch describes editable pitch and onset information. DrumScript documents a separate sheet engraving route that keeps a MusicXML handoff available. Audio recognition can lead to an editable note or groove representation. Check note starts, controllers and meter by ear before engraving or arranging. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Embodied and tactile interactive artSound2Hap’s authors report training and evaluating mappings from environmental audio to tactile signals. The performance mapping can be kept separate from model inference. Learned audio and gesture signals can become input to an embodied artwork. Rehearse that mapping and retain explicit fallback controls. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3

Archive the source documentation for model-assisted work. Face, speech and background identity each need hand review. 2 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. The CanonCGT research describes a reference-color transform for images with a different use scope. Check reference and target lighting, skin tones and consistency at shot boundaries. Learned film, tape and audio restorationThe cited video restoration research and MMagic documentation describe learned restoration on digitized inputs. Keep original fields, timing and a separate record of reconstructed color. Compare restoration against original fields and retain the capture. A restored color reconstruction is a separate interpretation. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3

Maintain a corrected source-language cut and an independently timed translated caption track. Model-language coverage and transcription quality depend on the clip. Comic lettering and localizationKoharu documents vertical and horizontal text fitting and a prior OCR/inpainting stage. Keep the scan, text-free layer and proofed reading order aligned so a letterer can revise translated dialogue without reconstructing the page. 4 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Neural capture of surface reflectanceThe CVPR light-propagation authors model light transport when estimating shape and appearance. The nvdiffrec authors show relighting with extracted material maps and known capture inputs. MaterialX documents an interchange representation for shader graphs. A research result under controlled lighting and a production-ready PBR material set require different validation. Keep capture assumptions, geometry and material channels explicit. 4 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Model-assisted auralization and scene acousticsThe Neural Acoustic Fields authors condition a room response on listener and emitter position. SoundSpaces documents a separate simulation route. SRERS publishes learned late-response synthesis with spatial early reflections as an input. Archive source and listener positions alongside channel layout and sample rate. Compare the estimated response with a measured or simulated reference when that exists. 8 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
AI-assisted tactile graphics and reliefsText2TactileGraphics shows learned depth/normal-map design and fabrication-aware reliefs, including reported reader feedback. AltCanvas explores image composition with spoken interaction. Both are research evidence; their paper or project page alone does not verify a redistributable software implementation. An image, outline or height map still needs tactile legibility, label spacing and an output-device check by the intended readers. 4 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. How it uses AI

StemScribe uses local HTDemucs stem separation, ONNX audio models and other tools to prepare separate repairs on vocals, drums, bass and accompaniment. [1] [3] [4]

Introduction

StemScribe uses local HTDemucs stem separation, ONNX audio models and other tools to prepare separate repairs on vocals, drums, bass and accompaniment. [1] [3] [4]

What it is good for

Compare a cleaned recording with its original at matched loudness and export a reviewed 24-bit WAV or editable musical reference. [1] [3] [4]

Demo & examples

The publisher reports timings on an Apple M4, shows the mixer and describes a matched-loudness comparison. The results are publisher observations from the named v0.10 build. [1] [3] [4]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Use the project’s published Apple Silicon release and check its exact build status. Select documented model downloads or import their corresponding local ONNX files.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Import a cleared WAV, MP3, FLAC or M4A source. Review diagnosis, separate tracks and judge each repair with the original at matched loudness. Save the dry file and export a reviewed WAV.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [3] [4]

Hardware
The publisher recommends at least 8 GB of RAM on Apple Silicon. Storage varies by selected models and audio project.
Software
StemScribe on Apple Silicon, ONNX Runtime and the selected HTDemucs weights. Optional transcription or quality-scoring engines have separate model requirements.
Platforms
Publisher scope is Apple Silicon macOS 13 or newer. Intel Mac, Windows and Linux authoring are undocumented.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [3] [4]

  • Weights: MIT application. The app documents MIT HTDemucs model variants. Review the distinct Audiobox scoring and other optional model grants before choosing them.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by MIT. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: Local processing requires storage and compute. HTDemucs ONNX is documented at about 166 MB per listed variant. No required subscription is documented for the local path.

Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [3] [4]

Limitations

The publisher’s release is a pre-release with ad hoc signing. Workflow sound quality, artifact handling and independent compatibility deserve separate checks. [1] [3] [4]

How it uses AI

The studio separates a cleared recording into WAV stems and converts an isolated instrument into editable MIDI with Basic Pitch. Optional audio models provide other source treatments. [1]

Introduction

The studio separates a cleared recording into WAV stems and converts an isolated instrument into editable MIDI with Basic Pitch. Optional audio models provide other source treatments. [1]

What it is good for

Prepare a drum loop and bass transcription for review in a DAW, with the files and a manifest moving together. [1]

Demo & examples

The German publisher guide gives a synthetic studio screenshot and a stem-to-DAW walkthrough. Check model separation, note curves and exact timing on real material. [1]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1]

  1. Follow the local Node 22, uv, FFmpeg with Opus, and Rubber Band requirements. The publisher describes a Python 3.11 backend and a locked dependency route.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1]

  1. Load an authorized song, separate its stems, take a two-bar passage and transcribe an isolated bass track. Correct note duration and bends before exporting selected WAV/MIDI with a manifest.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1]

Hardware
Node 22 and Python 3.11 are documented. Minimum RAM, VRAM and storage are undocumented.
Software
Browser studio and FastAPI backend plus the documented processing dependencies and specific Basic Pitch or separation assets. Optional cloud routes use a separate deployment.
Platforms
Local browser-based workflow with native tools behind it. The repository documents the service stack rather than a single verified OS/device matrix.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1]

  • Cost: Local tools and exports are described as usable without an online account. Optional online processing uses separately configured Modal credentials and service charges.

How it uses AI

This pipeline uses learned speech recognition, contextual translation and synthetic speech to produce time-constrained Bengali dubs. A web studio retains sentences for human review. [1]

Introduction

This pipeline uses learned speech recognition, contextual translation and synthetic speech to produce time-constrained Bengali dubs. A web studio retains sentences for human review. [1]
